rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw means superfluous speech without useful purpose.
rows.anchor: فضول الكلام ومالا طائل تحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's freedom from idle speech teaches people to avoid it even though Paradise has no legal duties.
rows.anchor: حيث نزه الله عنه الدار التي لا تكليف فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: If greetings among inhabitants or angels count as idle speech, they are the only idle words heard there.
rows.anchor: إن كان تسليم بعضهم على بعض أو تسليم الملائكة عليهم لغوا ، فلا يسمعون لغوا إلا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He likens that reading to a poet's praise of men whose only flaw is dents in their swords from battle.
rows.anchor: بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: Paradise hears only speech free of fault and deficiency.
rows.anchor: لا يسمعون فيها إلا قولا يسلمون فيه من العيب والنقيصة ، على الاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, salām is a prayer for safety; in the abode of safety its apparent redundancy is redeemed by the honor it conveys.
rows.anchor: معنى السلام هو الدعاء بالسلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People differ between one meal, eating whenever food appears (a glutton's habit), and the praised middle custom of lunch and dinner.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يأكل متى وجد وهي عادة المنهومين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise has no actual night or day; meal times are an approximation based on Arab usage for the well-provided.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون ثم ليل ولا نهار ، ولكن على التقدير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Morning and evening may instead mean provision that continues perpetually, as in ordinary speech about being with someone morning and evening.
rows.anchor: أراد دوام الرزق ودروره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading نورث is a metaphor: God leaves Paradise to the pious as an heir inherits an estate.
rows.anchor: استعارة ، أي : نبقي عليه الجنة كما نبقي على الوارث مال المورث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious meet God after their deeds end, while their deeds' fruit remains; entering Paradise is their inheritance from piety.
rows.anchor: يلقون ربهم يوم القيامة قد انقضت أعمالهم وثمرتها باقية وهي الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They inherit the dwellings in Paradise that would have belonged to the people of Hell had they obeyed.
rows.anchor: أورثوا من الجنة المساكن التي كانت لأهل النار لو أطاعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are Gabriel's explanation for his delayed descent when the Prophet was waiting for him.
rows.anchor: حكاية قول جبريل صلوات الله عليه حين استبطأه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel was detained forty days; another says fifteen, after questions about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit.
rows.anchor: أنه احتبس أربعين يوما . وقيل : خمسة عشر يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists said the Prophet's Lord had abandoned and detested him; the verse and Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā then came down.
rows.anchor: وقال المشركون : ودعه ربه وقلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel's delay distressed him and that he missed him; Gabriel replied that he too longed for him but was only commanded, descending when sent and waiting when detained.
rows.anchor: أبطأت حتى ساء ظني واشتقت إليك . قال : إني كنت أشوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanazzul can mean gradual descent or descent generally; a cited poem supports the sense of descending from the sky, and gradual descent best fits here.
rows.anchor: تنزل من جو السماء يصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend only at intervals when God commands, as He judges wise and prudent.
rows.anchor: في الأحايين وقتاغب وقت ليس إلا بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is before, behind, and between the angels means all directions and places; they cannot move from one place to another without the King's command.
rows.anchor: من الجهات والأماكن { وما بين ذالك } وما نحن فيها فلا نتمالك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrases may denote past worldly affairs, future afterlife affairs, and the forty-year interval between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: ما سلف من أمر الدنيا وما يستقبل من أمر الآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other glosses are elapsed and remaining lifetimes with the present state, what precedes existence and follows extinction, or earth, heaven, and what lies between.
rows.anchor: ما مضى من أعمارنا وما غبر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the glosses express God's encompassing knowledge: nothing is hidden from Him, so angelic action must follow His wisdom, command, and permission.
rows.anchor: المحيط بكل شيء لا تخفى عليه خافية ولا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord was not forgetful” means He did not abandon the Prophet; the delay awaited what was wise, as in the verse of al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وما كان تاركا لك ، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, these are the pious speaking on entering Paradise: they enter only by God's grace for their deeds, and He has not forgotten their recompense.
rows.anchor: هي حكاية قول المتقين حين يدخلون الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that alternative, God confirms that He does not forget workers' deeds, then the Prophet is told to worship and work so God may reward him like the pious.
rows.anchor: فحين عرفته على هذه الصفة ، فأقبل على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads يتنزل with yāʾ, relating the report to Gabriel, with the pronoun referring to revelation.
rows.anchor: بالياء على الحكاية عن جبريل عليه السلام والضمير للوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads إلا بقول ربك; the vocalic disagreement in النسي should match that in البغي.
rows.anchor: يجب أن يكون الخلاف في النسي مثله في البغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord of the heavens and earth” either apposes “your Lord” or predicates an omitted “He is.”
rows.anchor: بدل من ربك ، ويجوز أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second parsing, “worship Him” has the construction illustrated by the cited line about marrying the women of Khawlān.
rows.anchor: وقائلة خولان فانكح فتاتهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: With that parsing, “your Lord was not forgetful” may be the pious speaking, while the following words are God's speech.
rows.anchor: وما بعده من كلام رب العزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Persevere for His worship” takes lām rather than the usual ʿalā because worship is treated like an opponent in battle whom one must withstand.
rows.anchor: لأن العبادة جعلت بمنزلة القرن في قولك للمحارب : اصطبر لقرنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship brings hardships, so remain firm and do not lose heart at scriptural sophistries, delayed revelation, or the polytheists' gloating.
rows.anchor: العبادة تورد عليك شدائد ومشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No thing is truly named Allah; unlike idols called gods, this name belongs uniquely to the true deity.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون لأصنامهم آلهة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no one besides God is called al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: لا يسمى أحد الرحمن غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, no one bears His name truthfully; a false naming counts as no naming at all.
rows.anchor: هل تعلم من سمي باسمه على الحق دون الباطل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Samiyy may mean peer or likeness; since only God is worthy of worship, worship and perseverance are necessary.
rows.anchor: مثلا وشبيها ، أي : إذا صح أن لا معبود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” may mean all humankind or only some disbelievers; speech by some members of a kind can be attributed to the whole kind.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يراد بالإنسان الجنس بأسره ، وأن يراد بعض الجنس وهم الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports collective attribution with a line by al-Farazdaq: the blow is attributed to Banū ʿAbs though Warqāʾ ibn Zuhayr actually struck.
rows.anchor: فقد أسند الضرب إلى بني عبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal إذا is governed by an omitted verb indicated by أخرج, since the lām makes direct government by أخرج impossible.
rows.anchor: بفعل مضمر يدل عليه المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām can accompany the future because it is stripped down to pure emphasis, just as the hamza in يا الله loses its original defining force.
rows.anchor: لم تجامعها إلا مخلصة للتوكيد كما أخلصت الهمزة في يا الله للتعويض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added ما also emphasizes the incredulous question: can we really be brought out alive once death and ruin have taken us?
rows.anchor: قالوا : أحقا أنا سنخرج أحياء حين يتمكن فينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened emergence may mean being brought out of earth or out of extinction; sarcastically it may mean emerging alive as an exceptional marvel.
rows.anchor: الخروج من الأرض ، أو من حال الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Abū Ḥaywa read لسوف أخرج; Ṭalḥa reads لسأخرج, like Ibn Masʿūd's reading of a lām-prefixed future form in al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو حيوة : ( لسوف أخرج )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase is fronted under the particle of denial because life after death is the time they find most unbelievable.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الظرف وإيلاؤه حرف الإنكار من قبل أن ما بعد الموت هو وقت كون الحياة منكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following clause is coordinated with يقول despite the intervening interrogative hamza: how can he say this without recalling the first creation?
rows.anchor: لا يذكرون } على { يقول } ووسطت همزة الإنكار بين المعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First creation from nothing, with wise composition and no model, is more extraordinary than reassembling existing parts after their separation.
rows.anchor: حيث أخرج الجواهر والأعراض من العدم إلى الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “when he was nothing” supports the argument, as does 30:27; God's power is equal for both creations and needs no model or aid.
rows.anchor: على أن رب العزة سواء عليه النشأتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers except Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim use the doubled form لا يذكرون; Ubayy reads يتذكر.
rows.anchor: بالتشديد إلا نافعا وابن عامر وعاصما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before” means before the person's present state of continued life.
rows.anchor: الحالة التي هو فيها وهي حالة بقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's oath by His name joined to the Prophet's Lord honors and elevates the Prophet, as another oath honors heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: مضافا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : تفخيم لشأن رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction with “the devils” can mean “and” or “with”; “with” better conveys the disbelievers being paired with the devils who misled them, each chained to one.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم يحشرون مع قرنائهم من الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if humankind means everyone, the gathering is still with devils because everyone is gathered together and the disbelievers among them are paired with devils.
rows.anchor: إذا حشر جميع الناس حشرا واحدا وفيهم الكفرة مقرونين بالشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved and condemned are not separated at the gathering: the saved witness what God rescued them from and gain joy, while the enemies' grief and humiliation deepen.
rows.anchor: فيزدادوا لذلك غبطة إلى غبطة وسرورا إلى سرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the humans are specifically disbelievers, they are dragged from the gathering to Hell's edge on their knees, since those at the gathering are described as kneeling.
rows.anchor: جثاة على ركبهم ، غير مشاة على أقدامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kneeling may reflect customary tense, unsettled gatherings, with people crouching on mounts and readying themselves, or the inability to stand under terror.
rows.anchor: في مواقف المقاولات والمناقلات ، من تجاثي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the wording covers everyone, all crouch on reaching Hell; this is an anticipated state because kneeling accompanies the waiting before judgment and reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أنهم يتجاثون عند موافاة شاطيء جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A شيعة is a party following a misguiding leader; God distinguishes each faction's most disobedient and obstinate members for ordered punishment.
rows.anchor: تمتاز من كل طائفة من طوائف الغي والفساد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The most defiant may be the sect leaders, whose crime is doubled because they were both astray and misleaders; Qur'anic parallels describe their added burden and punishment.
rows.anchor: رؤساء الشيع وأئمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl parses أيهم as quoted speech, meaning those of whom it is asked which is most defiant; Sibawayh builds it on ḍamm after omission of its relative clause's initial element.
rows.anchor: لننزعن الذين يقال فيهم أيهم أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes the removal apply to some from every sect, with أيهم أشد answering the implied question “which ones?”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون النزع واقعا على { من كل شيعة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and Muʿādh ibn Muslim, al-Farrāʾ's teacher, read أيهم أشد in the accusative.
rows.anchor: بالنصب عن طلحة ابن مصرف وعن معاذ بن مسلم الهراء أستاذ الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositions in “most defiant against” and “more deserving of burning” are explanatory, or attach to the comparatives: their defiance and deserving of Hell are greater.
rows.anchor: عتوهم أشد على الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among you” may shift from the singular “human” to address people generally, supported by Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima's reading وإن منهم.
rows.anchor: يعضده قراءة ابن عباس وعكرمة رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If all humankind is meant, ورود means entering a quenched Hell: believers cross it while others fall through; Ibn ʿAbbās compares it to clarified fat.
rows.anchor: دخولهم فيها وهي جامدة ، فيعبرها المؤمنون

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet said the people of Paradise will be told they crossed the Fire while it was quenched, fulfilling the promise to reach it.
rows.anchor: سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك ؟

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir also reports the Prophet's explanation that everyone, righteous or wicked, enters it, but it is cool and safe for believers as it was for Abraham.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( الورود الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse saying the righteous are kept far from Hell means kept far from its punishment.
rows.anchor: أولئك عنها مبعدون } ( الأنبياء : 101 ) فالمراد عن عذابها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda identify arrival with crossing the bridge stretched over Hell.
rows.anchor: هو الجواز على الصراط ؛ لأن الصراط ممدود عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says something can approach without entering, as Moses approached Midian's water and a caravan may reach a town without entering it.
rows.anchor: قد يرد الشيء الشيء ولا يدخله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says a believer's arrival at Hell is fever touching his body in this world, citing the Prophetic saying that fever comes from Hell's breath.
rows.anchor: ورود المؤمن النار هو مس الحمى جسده في الدنيا ، بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that arrival means people kneeling around Hell; if only disbelievers are addressed, the meaning is straightforward.
rows.anchor: إن أريد الكفار خاصة ، فالمعنى بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥatm is the source of “to impose”; here it names the obligation God imposed on Himself and decreed as inevitable.
rows.anchor: مصدر حتم الأمر إذا أوجبه ، فسمى به الموجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saving verb has several active and passive readings; if everyone is meant, their deliverance is clear, but if only disbelievers are meant, the pious go to Paradise after them.
rows.anchor: على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Jaḥdarī, and Ibn Abī Laylā read ثم ننجى with fatḥ on thāʾ, meaning “there/at that point.”
rows.anchor: بفتح الثاء ، أي هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about leaving wrongdoers kneeling supports arrival as kneeling around Hell; believers then depart for Paradise while wrongdoers remain.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن المراد بالورود الجثو حواليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Clear” may mean well-articulated wording, concise meanings, evident aims, decisive or explained ambiguous verses, clarification by the Prophet, miracles, or proofs.
rows.anchor: مرتلات الألفاظ ، ملخصات المعاني : مبينات المقاصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest parsing treats “clear” as an emphatic circumstantial description, since God's signs are necessarily clear proofs.
rows.anchor: لأن آيات الله لا تكون إلا واضحة وحججا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking “to the believers” can mean addressing them directly or speaking for their sake, as in the parallel about unbelievers' claims.
rows.anchor: وأنهم يفوهون به لأجلهم وفي معناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqāman with ḍamma for a residence or home; the other reading with fatḥ means a place of standing; both mean location.
rows.anchor: بالضم وهو موضع الإقامة والمنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadī is the gathering place or assembly of a people, where they meet.
rows.anchor: المجلس ومجتمع القوم ، وحيث ينتدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignorant of more than worldly appearances, the disbelievers use prosperity as their measure of truth, asking which team has the better place and assembly.
rows.anchor: من المؤمنين بالآيات والجاحدين لها أوفر حظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they groomed, oiled, perfumed, and adorned themselves, boasting to poor Muslims that they were more honored by God.
rows.anchor: يروى أنهم كانوا يرجلون شعورهم ويدهنون ويتطيبون ويتزينون بالزين الفاخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “how many generations” is the object of أهلكنا, with “of generations” clarifying its ambiguity; each age is a generation relative to those after it.
rows.anchor: تبيين لإبهامها ، أي : كثيرا من القرون أهلكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They were better” is an accusative adjective describing كم; without the pronoun phrase, أحسن itself would need accusative adjective inflection.
rows.anchor: في محل النصب صفة لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athāth means household furnishings; another view restricts it to fine bedding, while khirthī means worn furnishings or garments.
rows.anchor: متاع البيت . وقيل : هو ماجد من الفرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Ṭūsī's poem uses athāth for household goods that have become worn, witnessing the contrast with khirthī.
rows.anchor: وصار أثاث البيت خرثيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings of رئيا include “appearance/form,” an inverted form, hamza-to-yāʾ with assimilation, and derivation from luxury and blessing.
rows.anchor: وهو المنظر والهيئة فعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further readings drop the hamza after shifting it, or read زيا from collected adornments; all mean the earlier generations looked better.
rows.anchor: وهو الجمع ؛ لأن الزي محاسن مجموعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Let the Merciful extend him” means grant respite and a longer life; the imperative signals this outcome's inevitability and removes the lost person's excuse.
rows.anchor: أمهله وأملى له في العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may instead be a prayer that God prolong the life of the one in error; another verse describes respite as increasing sin.
rows.anchor: في معنى الدعاء بأن يمهله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading connects the verse back to the unbelievers' boast, with two verses as an aside: they persist until witnessing the promised event.
rows.anchor: أن تكون متصلة بالآية التي هي رابعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that connection, the promised punishment is either worldly defeat, capture, and killing by Muslims, or humiliation at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: غلبة المسلمين عليهم وتعذيبهم إياهم قتلا وأسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that point they learn their rank is the reverse of their boast: a worse place and weaker forces than the believers.
rows.anchor: أنهم شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse connects forward: God prolongs those lost in misguidance because His knowledge shows that favors will not benefit them.
rows.anchor: أن الذين في الضلالة ممدود لهم في ضلالتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misguidance is the ignorance and excess in disbelief that led to their boast; they persist until seeing God's support for believers or the Hour's signs.
rows.anchor: ما دعاهم من جهلهم وغلوهم في كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clauses after حتى complete it; “place” corresponds to their dwelling and “assembly” to the meeting of their leaders and supporters.
rows.anchor: هي التي تحكى بعدها الجمل ألا ترى الجملة الشرطية واقعة بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويزيد is coordinated with the implied predicate position of فليمدد; God increases the lost in error by abandonment and the guided in guidance through enabling them.
rows.anchor: معطوف على موضع فليمدد ؛ لأنه واقع موقع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting good deeds may mean all afterlife deeds, ritual prayers, or the four formulas of praise and declaration; they out-reward the disbelievers' boasting.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الصلوات . وقيل : سبحان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Better return” means a better destination and outcome, or greater benefit.
rows.anchor: أي مرجعا وعاقبة ، أو منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the deeds a better reward is taunting irony: the disbelievers' boast leads to Hell, and such irony can sting more than a direct threat.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل : ثوابهم النار . على طريقة قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison remains idiomatic although the opponents have no share in good reward, like saying summer is hotter than winter means hotter in heat than winter is cold.
rows.anchor: هذا من وجيز كلامهم ، يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفرأيت means “report/tell”; the fāʾ links this disbeliever's story after the previous people's story.
rows.anchor: في معنى ( أخبر ) والفاء جاءت لإفادة معناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أطلع الغيب evokes climbing to a summit; the cited line by Jarīr witnesses مطلع for a mountain ascent, while the expression can mean mastering a matter.
rows.anchor: إذا ارتقى إلى أعلاه وطلع الثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His claim to future wealth and children requires either knowledge of the unseen or a covenant from its Knower, and the verse asks which he possesses.
rows.anchor: وإما عهد من عالم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ولدا as a plural of ولد or as a synonym for it; Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar has another kasra-vowelled reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي : ( ولدا )

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The covenant may mean the testimony of faith; Qatāda asks whether he has a righteous deed to rely on, while al-Kalbī asks whether God promised him the wealth.
rows.anchor: في العهد : كلمة الشهادة . وعن قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the passage was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, though the widely held view identifies al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن رحمه الله : نزلت في الوليد

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ owed him money and demanded that Khabāb disbelieve in Muḥammad before he would repay it; Khabāb refused even after death or resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرت : ( 674 ) كان لي عليه دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Khabāb's account, al-ʿĀṣ asks whether he will be resurrected and boasts he will then have wealth and children with which to pay.
rows.anchor: فإني إذا مت بعثت ؟ قلت : نعم . قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second report says Khabāb made jewelry for him and demanded payment; al-ʿĀṣ deferred it, claiming he would have gold, silver, and silk in Paradise.
rows.anchor: صاغ له خباب حليا فاقتضاه الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا is a rebuke and warning: he is mistaken in imagining and wishing this, and must stop.
rows.anchor: ردع وتنبيه على الخطأ أي : هو مخطيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although his words are already recorded, the future in سنكتب may mean God will reveal to him that they were recorded, as in a poem where lineage makes one's origins known.
rows.anchor: إذا ما انتسبنا لم تلدني لئيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a threat formula promising eventual vengeance even if punishment is delayed.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه لا يخل بالانتصار وإن تطاول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may lengthen the punishment appropriate to him or increase and multiply it; ʿAlī's reading ونمد with ḍamma supports the latter, reinforced by the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: أي نطول له من العذاب ما يستأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled punishment expresses the severity of God's anger.
rows.anchor: وذلك من فرط غضب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We inherit what he says” can mean stripping away the wealth and children he claims he will receive and giving them to someone deserving.
rows.anchor: نزوي عنه ما زعم أنه يناله في الآخرة ونعطيه من يستحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, what he says names his hoped-for wealth and children; even if granted in this life, they are ultimately taken from him and he comes alone.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه قد تمنى وطمع أن يؤتيه الله في الدنيا مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or he says this only while alive; death silences him, or God preserves the words in his record to expose and shame him at the gathering.
rows.anchor: ما دام حيا ، فإذا قبضناه حلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He comes poor and alone, deprived of wealth, children, and his wish, bearing both the consequences of his boast and the loss of what he coveted.
rows.anchor: من المال والولد ، لم نوله سؤله ولم نؤته متمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, “alone” describes a state everyone shares on arrival before their later outcomes diverge.
rows.anchor: حال مقدرة نحو { فادخلوها خالدين } لأنه وغيره سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters took gods as عزّاً to gain strength through supposed intercession and support before God.
rows.anchor: أي ليتعززوا بآلهتهم حيث يكونون لهم عند الله شفعاء وأنصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes their reliance on the idols; a reported reading of كلا is discussed, and Ibn Jinnī records a vocalized form meaning “all this opinion.”
rows.anchor: ردع لهم وإنكار لتعززهم بالآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they will deny” may refer to the idols, who disavow worshippers, as in the verse about partners calling their worshippers liars.
rows.anchor: للآلهة ، أي : سيجحدون عبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it refers to the idolaters, who deny having worshipped them after their evil end.
rows.anchor: ينكرون لسوء العاقبة أن يكونوا قد عبدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضد contrasts with عزّ: the idols become humiliation, the opposite of the protection sought; ضد can also mean helper because a helper opposes one's enemy.
rows.anchor: ضد العز وهو الذل والهوان ، أي : يكونون عليهم ضدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular ضداً represents the idol group as one through their agreement, like the Prophetic saying that they are one hand against outsiders.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( 676 ) ( وهم يد على من سواهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As helpers against them, idols become fuel and kindling of Hell and the reason their worshippers are punished.
rows.anchor: أنهم وقود النار وحصب جهنم ، ولأنهم عذبوا بسبب عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to the polytheists, they themselves become enemies and deniers after having worshipped the idols.
rows.anchor: أي : كفرة ، بعد أن كانوا يعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azz, hazz, and istifzāz all mean agitation and forceful disturbance: devils incite sins through whispering and alluring suggestions.
rows.anchor: الأز ، والهز ، والاستفزاز : أخوات ، ومعناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves the disbelievers with the devils rather than restraining them, though He could stop them by force.
rows.anchor: خلينا بينهم وبينهم ولم نمنعهم ولو شاء لمنعهم قسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage makes the Prophet marvel at the obstinate disbelievers' excess, mockery, resistance to clear truth, and immersion in Satan's prompting.
rows.anchor: من تماديهم في الغي وإفراطهم في العناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not hurry God to destroy them for relief from their harm; only a count of days and breaths remains before the desired end.
rows.anchor: لا تعجل عليهم بأن يهلكوا ويبيدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their remaining time passes as swiftly as the moment spent counting it, like the verse describing their life as an hour of a day.
rows.anchor: فليس بينك وبين ما تطلب من هلاكهم إلا أيام محصورة وأنفاس معدودة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās wept while reciting this and said the last count is one's last breath, parting from family, and entering the grave.
rows.anchor: آخر العدد خروج نفسك ، آخر العدد فراق أهلك

rows.speaker: ابن السماك
rows.claim: At al-Maʾmūn's court, Ibn al-Sammāk observed that numbered breaths without extension are quickly exhausted.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت الأنفاس بالعدد ولم يكن لها مدد ، فما أسرع ما تنفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم is accusative under an omitted verb (“on the day We gather and drive,” or “remember the day”), or it can depend on لا يملكون.
rows.anchor: ونسوق : نفعل بالفريقين ما لا يحيط به الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are described honorifically as gathering to their merciful Lord like delegations visiting kings in expectation of honor.
rows.anchor: ذكر المتقون بلفظ التبجيل . وهو أنهم يجمعون

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports that they are carried on camels with gold litters and ruby saddles rather than walking on foot.
rows.anchor: ما يحشرون والله على أرجلهم ، ولكنهم على نوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals are driven to Hell in humiliation like thirsty livestock driven to water; ورد means thirsty, while its root sense is journeying to water.
rows.anchor: كأنهم نعم عطاش تساق إلى الماء . والورد : العطاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poem about a bird going to water witnesses the word's water-journey sense.
rows.anchor: ردي ردي ورد قطاة صما … كدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads يحشر المتقون and يساق المجرمون in the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( يحشر المتقون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural marker in لا يملكون may be a pronoun referring to the servants, or a plural suffix like أكلوني البراغيث; من اتخذ is generic and may be nominative as apposition or subject.
rows.anchor: الواو في { لا يملكون } إن جعل ضميرا فهو للعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من اتخذ may instead be accusative after eliding the annexed noun, meaning “except the intercession of one who took a covenant.”
rows.anchor: على تقدير حذف المضاف ، أي إلا شفاعة من اتخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not possess the right to intercede for someone; taking a covenant means securing faith and righteous action.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون أن يشفع لهم ، واتخاذ العهد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports a Prophetic instruction to make a covenant morning and evening through a confession of God's oneness, Muḥammad's messengership, dependence on mercy, and a prayer for a pledge kept at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه ذات يوم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The covenant may simply be the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: كلمة الشهادة . أو يكون من ( عهد الأمير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is an authorization to intercede: only those whom God commands and permits may do so.
rows.anchor: أي لا يشفع إلا المأمور بالشفاعة المأذون له فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إدّ is read with kasra or fatḥa; Ibn Khālawayh glosses it as astonishing, while other views call it grave and objectionable or severe.
rows.anchor: قال ابن خالويه : الإد والأد : العجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kisāʾī and Nāfiʿ read يكاد with yāʾ; another reading has ينفطرن, whose repeated form means being split apart, unlike the simpler انفطار.
rows.anchor: والتفطر : من فطره إذا شققه وكرر الفعل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ينصدعن; هداً may be an emphatic verbal noun, a passive participle, or a causal accusative explaining why they split.
rows.anchor: أي تهد هدا ، أو مهدودة ، أو مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God nearly would have split the heavens, earth, and mountains in anger at the claim, but His forbearance prevents haste; 35:41 is a parallel.
rows.anchor: كدت أفعل هذا بالسموات والأرض والجبال عند وجود هذه الكلمة غضبا مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the cosmic collapse dramatizes the enormity of the utterance and its destruction of religion's foundations through an image of physical damage.
rows.anchor: أن يكون استعظاما للكلمة ، وتهويلا من فظاعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to direct address in لقد جئتم after third-person narration intensifies censure and warns of the enormity and audacity of their statement.
rows.anchor: من المخاطبة بعد الغيبة ، وهو الذي يسمى الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن دعوا may be genitive as an apposition to منه, accusative after eliding lām, or nominative as the subject of هداً; each links the collapse to their ascription of a child.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة أوجه : أن يكون مجرورا بدلا من الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeatedly naming al-Raḥmān underscores that only He deserves the name: all blessings originate from Him, and attributing a child makes Him like creation.
rows.anchor: أنه هو الرحمن وحده ، لا يستحق هذا الاسم غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دعوا may mean “named,” with the first object omitted to generalize every being called a child, or “attributed,” as in the report and poetic example continued next.
rows.anchor: المتعدي إلى مفعولين ، فاقتصر على أحدهما

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet's phrase من ادعى إلى غير مواليه witnesses دعى in the sense of claiming or attributing lineage.
rows.anchor: من ادعى إلى غير مواليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet says “we do not claim descent to a father,” illustrating دعا بمعنى نسب.
rows.anchor: إنا بني نهشل لا ندعي لأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: انبغى means something sought or attainable; taking a child is impossible for God, whether by biological birth or adoption, since adoption presupposes the same kind and God has no genus.
rows.anchor: ما يتأتى له اتخاذ الولد وما ينطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janaḥ ibn Ḥubaysh reads ودّ with kasra; God creates affection for believers in hearts without their courting it or using ordinary causes such as kinship, friendship, or favors.
rows.anchor: بالكسر : والمعنى : سيحدث لهم في القلوب مودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future may refer to the Makkan believers' later rise from being hated, or to Resurrection, when their good deeds are displayed and win them love.
rows.anchor: والسين إما لأن السورة مكية وكان المؤمنون حينئذ ممقوتين بين الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet told ʿAlī to ask God for a covenant and affection in believers' hearts, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال لعلي رضي الله عنه : ( 680 ) ( يا علي قل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God loves the believers and makes His creatures love them.
rows.anchor: يعني يحبهم الله ويحببهم إلى خلقه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God tells Gabriel that He loves someone; Gabriel and the heavens then love him, and love is placed for him among people on earth.
rows.anchor: يا جبريل قد أحببت فلانا فأحبه ، فيحبه جبريل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says when a servant turns toward God, God turns people's hearts toward that servant.
rows.anchor: ما أقبل العبد إلى الله إلا أقبل الله بقلوب العباد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the sura's conclusion: relay the revelation, which God made easy and clear in the Prophet's eloquent Arabic, to give good news and warning.
rows.anchor: خاتمة السورة ومقطعها ، فكأنه قال : بلغ هذا المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ludd are fierce disputants in falsehood, taking every side of argument through obstinacy; the intended people are Meccans.
rows.anchor: الشداد الخصومة بالباطل ، الآخذون في كل لديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of earlier generations is a threat and warning to the Meccans.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وكم أهلكنا } تخويف لهم وإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تحس means perceive or sense; Ḥanẓala reads تسمع as the present of أسمعت, “hear.”
rows.anchor: إذا شعر به . ومنه الحواس والمحسوسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rikz is a faint sound; the related word rakāz means buried treasure, from the image of a spear point set into earth.
rows.anchor: الصوت الخفي . ومنه : ركز الرمح

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds for each named prophet and believer who denied or affirmed them, and for those who supplicate or do not supplicate, to whoever recites Sūrat Maryam.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 682 ) ( من قرأ سورة مريم
